context:
Pre-registered D1 criteria. Confirm or change them with the maintainer BEFORE running the replay, record the confirmed values in this item, and do not change them after seeing results:
- Recall: 100% on the known-regression commits and on every attributable canary failure since 2026-09-14 (first failing day per test). Any miss is a no-go until the selector is fixed and the replay is rerun.
- Cost, per placement:
  - (a) trunk.yml: mean estimated runner-minutes per merge at most 40 (the full suite is about 100), and p90 wall time at most 30 minutes.
  - (b) ci.yml on pull_request: the same two limits, measured per PR head push, not per merge, because each push to a PR runs the jobs.
- Whole-suite fallback rate reported. Above 30% of merges, the savings case is weak; report it for the maintainer rather than tuning the fallback away.

Trunk backlog context for placement (a): trunk run 37981829409 had jobs queued about 2.5 hours on 2026-10-09 (trunk.yml uses queue: max concurrency). Added trunk jobs share that queue, so report the observed queue delay next to the wall-time numbers.

Guardrails:
1. Read-only against the repository: use temporary worktrees or git archive; never modify develop or push.
2. Report every miss with the merge, the failing test, and the missing edge. Do not tune thresholds, exclude merges, or weaken fail-safe rules to pass.
3. Commit the harness and a durable report under _project/analysis/ with the exact merge SHAs used, so the numbers can be replayed.
4. If a failure cannot be attributed to one merge, record it as unattributed with the evidence; do not count it as a hit.

description:
Measure the selector against history before any CI wiring. Validation must use the dependency map as it existed before each merge: a map built from today's tree says nothing about what would have been selected then.

Build a replay harness that, for each of about the last 60 develop merges (and every known-regression commit), checks out the merge's parent tree, builds the selector map there, applies that merge's exact diff, and records: selected node IDs, whether a whole-suite fallback fired and why, and estimated runner-minutes and wall time from measured per-test durations plus per-shard setup (from canary-impact-01-junit-durations), using the selector's shard sizing (about 10 minutes of tests per shard, 1 to 6 shards).

Also replay every daily canary failure since 2026-09-14: for each failing test, find the merge that introduced the failure and check the selector selected that test on that merge. Count a test only on the first day it fails; later failing days of the same test are not new attributions. The release canary failed 24 of 26 scheduled runs since 2026-09-14, so this set is large and many days repeat the same tests.

DECISION POINT D1 (maintainer): two decisions, recorded together.
1. Placement. The merge queue was retired on 2026-10-03, so the shadow job (canary-impact-04-shadow-job) and any later gate (canary-impact-06-required-gate) must run in one of two places:
   (a) post-merge in .github/workflows/trunk.yml, on each develop push; or
   (b) pre-merge in .github/workflows/ci.yml, on pull_request.
2. Go or no-go for the shadow job at the chosen placement.
The agent reports the numbers for both placements and stops; it does not start item 04.
